newsitem.title: USA: Texas ups sales tax rebates to cities, counties.
newsitem.headline: Texas ups sales tax rebates to cities, counties.

text.p: Sales tax rebates to Texas cities and counties from the state jumped more than seven percent in July compared with the same month last year, officials said Friday.
State comptroller John Sharp said in a statement he paid back $140 million to 1,086 Texas cities, up 7.4 percent from $130.3 million paid in July of 1996.
Another $13.6 million was paid to 117 counties, up 7.6 percent from $12.6 million in the year-ago period.
So far this year, sales tax rebates to cities and counties are up 5.7 percent from the same period in 1996.

The money owed to the cities and counties represents amounts collected in excess of the state's sales tax limit of 6.25 percent by retailers in their jurisdiction. Texas has no income tax, and uses sales tax for revenues.
July's rebates derive from local taxes collected on May sales and reported to the state in June by businesses filing monthly returns.
Sharp said the rise in rebates reflects continuing economic growth, "Consumers continue to show confidence in the rising employment numbers and robust rate of growth of the Texas economy."
Among the larger cities receiving rebates, Houston got $18.2 million, up 7.8 percent from last year. Its year-to-date payments are up 3.8 percent.
Dallas received $12.1 million, down two percent from last year. But year-to-date payments are up 1.9 percent.
San Antonio's allocations in July rose 6.4 percent to $7.9 million. The city is averaging an increase of 4.7 percent on a year-to-date basis.
Fort Worth's share jumped 11.3 percent to $3.8 million for July, and is averaging a five percent increase so for this year.
